body: Registry is pure (no IO, no async) and owned by one Slots actor; every Telegram answer returns as a Done message on the actor's own channel, so ingress keeps draining during retry_after. Alternative: Arc<Mutex<Registry>> with Telegram awaited inline on the ingress loop (the TASK-010 QA failure mode).

Topic calls come from one diff, Registry::topic_work: desired title/icon vs applied_title/applied_icon per slot, busy flag per slot, failed marker until retry_every. Alternative: each event emits its own create/edit effects (duplicate edits, harder to guarantee exactly one replacement after TOPIC_ID_INVALID).

Nesting is decided on the hub from the existing wire field HookEvent::SessionStart.parent_claude_pid plus a persisted pids map '<host>/<claude_pid>' -> session_id: unknown pid = Nested{parent: None}, pid of the session itself = TopLevel. No wire change; TASK-012 only fills claude_pid/parent_claude_pid. Alternative: the device sends a nesting enum or parent session id (needs the hub registry on the device anyway, bumps the contract).

No separator for the first session of a brand-new slot; a separator only when a slot's current session changes to another id. Alternative: separator on every occupancy (acceptance 1 would see two separators in the topic).

Slot allocation order: slot the session already holds; its previous slot if free (resume keeps the topic); slot of the previous session of the same host+claude_pid in the same folder (/clear), which that session gives up; first free ordinal; new ordinal. Alternative: plain first-free (a /clear or resume can jump to another topic).
An unparsable or foreign-version registry.json stops `cctg hub` with a fixed-text error; a missing file is an empty registry. Alternative: start empty (every folder silently gets a second topic).

After start, topic edits wait a 45 s grace (> agent max backoff 30 s) while creations and separators go out at once. Alternative: edit immediately (every live slot flips to no-channel and back after each hub restart, plus two service messages each).

An agent whose session the registry does not know waits hook_wait=10 s for its SessionStart hook, then the session is adopted as top-level; UserPromptSubmit/Stop of an unknown session also adopt it. Alternative: never give agent-only sessions a slot (a session started while the hub was down would stay invisible, contradicting TASK-018).

Every forum_topic_edited service message whose thread is a slot topic is deleted; nothing is deleted when the bot lacks can_delete_messages (startup warning is the one log), and the first runtime delete failure warns once. Alternative: count expected edits per topic and delete only those (fragile when an edit's service message is lost or reordered).

Icons alive/dead/waiting/no_channel = 5312016608254762256 (lightning) / 5408906741125490282 (chequered flag) / 5377316857231450742 (question mark) / 5357121491508928442 (eyes) from a read-only getForumTopicIconStickers call (112 stickers, 2026-09-23); the hub re-checks them at start and drops any id Telegram no longer offers. Alternative: env-configurable ids (a knob nobody asked for).

Title limit 128 is measured with transcript::telegram_len (UTF-16 units, >= chars); label cut first, then folder, host capped at 32, ' #N' always kept. Alternative: chars().count() (an emoji title could exceed Telegram's count).

SlotLocator answers /brief and /full in a slot topic without a prefix from the registry view (watch channel); General, prefixes and unknown topics keep ProjectsDir. New LocateError::NoTranscript for an agent-only session. Alternative: registry-only locator (breaks /brief in General and prefix lookups of pre-registry sessions).

First slots actor tests sent a hook and an agent registration back to back and expected hook-first order; tokio::select! picks among ready channels at random, so the agent was sometimes handled first (pending, then bound) and the op count differed. Tests now wait for the hook's op before sending the agent; production relies on the pending/hook_wait path for exactly this reorder.
Mutation 'separator for the first session of a new slot' survives: topic_created clears pending_separator, so the mutant is behaviourally equivalent; no test can kill it.

Self-resolving parent pid (pids[parent] == this session): classify the start as NestedUnknownParent and return Parent(None) WITHOUT rewriting the existing session record. Alternative rejected: overwrite entry.kind/slot with Nested{None} (PLAN_V2 literal) - a known top-level session would lose its slot and keep the nested kind on every later plain resume.

One topic call per slot in flight (Create > Separator > Edit, separator sets busy and stays pending until success; stale results for another thread id are full no-ops). Alternative rejected: per-job generation tokens - with a single in-flight job per slot every live result matches, tokens add state without closing another hole.

Ingress isolation via an unbounded dispatch channel to a dispatch task that awaits Outbox::submit; the actor has no await outside its inputs. Alternative rejected: changing scheduler.rs QUEUE_CAPACITY or try_send with drop - touches TASK-008 code, and dropping topic jobs would lose desired state.

First repro of the TOPIC_ID_INVALID double replacement used SessionEnd then SessionStart as two events; the dead-icon edit consumed the injected error and each event pumped separately, so the race did not show (test passed on the buggy code). Switched to /clear (one SessionStart with the same claude pid) so separator and title edit are issued in one pass: reproduced 3/3.

Verdict NEEDS_WORK instead of PASS although all 10 acceptance criteria hold: the planned /clear rule (same claude_pid keeps its slot) only works when SessionStart reaches the hub before SessionEnd, and a nested start permanently rewrites a known top-level session's kind; both reproduced by probe tests. Alternative rejected: PASS with the two as follow-ups (the /clear order is the normal one, so the plan's own invariant fails in practice).

I1 /clear hand-off: SessionEnd(reason=clear) of a top-level session records host/pid -> slot for 60 s (only if the pid is not already taken by the next session); SessionStart(source=clear) of that pid prefers the slot if it is free and in the same folder. Alternative rejected: the review's 'free slot whose last session had the same claude_pid' with no TTL or reason check, which lets a reused Windows pid steer an unrelated startup session away from the first free ordinal.

I4 delivery==None handled as topic_failed (retried on the retry tick) and Registry::release removed as now unused. Alternative rejected: stopping the slot worker, which would also stop hook/agent ingress handling for a condition that only a scheduler panic can cause.

I5 incremental ai-title scan: actor keeps session -> (path, offset of complete lines); read_title seeks there; a trailing line without newline is rescanned next time; entry dropped on title found or SessionEnd. Alternative rejected: time throttle per session, which still rereads the whole file each time.

First QA e2e harness drove Slots through Scheduler with BucketConfig::default() and settled after 250 ms without new ops; a second separator waits the 1 s min_gap, so s9 (compact then resume) failed 1 of 3 runs with the resumed separator missing. Not a product bug: harness now uses capacity 1000, refill 1 ms, min_gap 0.

Verdict NEEDS_FIXES although all 10 acceptance criteria pass: a nested run's SessionEnd marks a live top-level session ended and its topic goes to the next session (s5b, s5c), and a normal startup with a reused pid inherits a stale slot after a lost SessionEnd (s4b), which the orchestrator named as a must-not. Alternative rejected: SHIP with both as known limitations (the first breaks one-live-session-per-topic, the second is an explicit QA check).

B1: SessionEnd gains optional claude_pid; the hub ignores it only when both the event pid and the session's recorded claude_pid are present and differ. Alternative rejected: the QA wording 'pid present and != entry.claude_pid', which never ends a session whose SessionStart carried no pid once hooks start sending pids.

B2: allocate takes the pids hand-off only for source=clear (clear_pid); for any other start a pids entry of another session marks that session ended before allocation, so the start takes the first free slot. Alternative rejected: dropping the stale marking and leaving the crashed session's slot busy until a later SessionEnd that never comes.

O1 kept as a documented limitation (code comment at the separator failure branch). Alternative rejected: a bounded retry, which needs a new per-slot attempt counter and a policy for dropping an undelivered separator, beyond a small fix.
